The oil subsidy, which too has soared, will also need to be settled, although not immediately.The Rs 1.9 lakh crore push for electronics manufacturing will require some additional allocation this year and with other ministries also drawing up replacement schemes for production linked incentive, some of which may have to wait, given the pressure on expenditure.For a govt that has stuck to the fiscal deficit targets, despite facing one pressure or another almost every year, Sitharaman will seek to maintain her record and achieve the goal of 4.3% of GDP.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman may seek Parliamentary approval for additional spending. The fertiliser subsidy, other West Asia related spends and initiatives, such as the electronics manufacturing push through schemes for semiconductors and mobiles adding to the Centre’s expenditure.

Article Title: 14 killed, many missing as flash floods, landslides ravage J&K’s Poonch, Rajouri
Article Text:
Poonch: Residents gather in the aftermath of torrential rain-triggered landslides and flash floods, at Dhara Sangla village of Surankote tehsil, in Poonch district, Jammu and Kashmir. At least 12 people were killed and several others missing as rains unleashed landslides and flash floods across the twin border districts of Poonch and Rajouri in the union territory on Sunday, causing widespread damage to public and private infrastructure including roads and houses, officials said. (PTI Photo)

JAMMU: Torrential rain unleashed flash floods and landslides in Pir Panjal region of J&K’s Poonch and Rajouri districts Sunday, killing at least 14 people, leaving several missing and burying homes under walls of water, rock and mud that barrelled down mountain slopes. Officials said the toll could rise as rescuers searched for those trapped beneath debris.CM Omar Abdullah cut short his stay in New Delhi and flew to Jammu to oversee relief operations after heavy rain triggered widespread devastation in the two border districts. Police, Army, SDRF, civil administration and local volunteers fanned out across worst-hit Surankote, Haveli and Mandi in Poonch, while LG Manoj Sinha reviewed rescue efforts and directed immediate relief for affected families.Heavy rain disrupted traffic on strategic Jammu-Srinagar NH-44, prompting authorities to urge commuters to avoid vulnerable stretches. Annual Amarnath Yatra, which began July 3, and pilgrimages to Vaishno Devi shrine in Katra and Shiv Khori in Reasi were temporarily suspended after IMD forecast adverse weather for the next three days.Officials said Lower Murrah in Surankote suffered the heaviest loss, where eight members of a family were swept away.Two bodies had been found by evening while search teams continued to retrieve the remaining six. The dead included Noor Safia, 59; her sons Sajad Ahmed, 16, Haqnawaz Ahmed, 10, and Shahnawaz Ahmed, 10; Khalda Kouser, 25, and her 2-year-old son Sofian; Bano Bi, 60; and Mohammad Akram, 7.Four more died in Sangla village, while a fatality is also reported from nearby Sangalani. Nazia Kouser, 28, died in Noona Bandi, and four injured were shifted to Poonch district hospital.LG Sinha said he had spoken to senior officials and reviewed rescue operations. “Affected families have been moved to safety. All departments are on high alert,” he said. “I urge residents to stay calm and follow official updates. I am deeply saddened by the loss of lives in Rajouri and Poonch.”CM Abdullah expressed grief over the deaths, offered condolences to bereaved families and prayed for those injured. His office said he had remained in constant touch with local MLAs before flying to Jammu to personally monitor the situation.Former CM Ghulam Nabi Azad also condoled the loss of lives and widespread destruction.Rescue teams pulled three boys to safety near Peer Kho temple in Jammu after Tawi swelled suddenly. In Rajouri, Army, police and SDRF rescued two boys stranded in flooded Dhangri riverbank and nine others marooned in Thanamandi.Army’s White Knight Corps said troops “braving challenging flood conditions and swift water currents” rescued 11 civilians, including five children.Authorities sounded a flood alert across Jammu division after water levels surged in Chenab and other rivers. Gates of Salal hydroelectric project in Reasi remained open for a second day during reservoir flushing, sharply increasing discharge into Chenab. Police in neighbouring Ramban also issued an advisory after gates of Baglihar hydroelectric project were opened, sending river levels higher.
Article Summary: Torrential rain unleashed flash floods and landslides in Pir Panjal region of J&K’s Poonch and Rajouri districts Sunday, killing at least 14 people. Officials said the toll could rise as rescuers searched for those trapped beneath debris.

Article Title: NEET cutoff at record high, qualifiers shrink by 1.1 lakh+
Article Text:
Highest Success Rate In EWS; 9% Skipped Retest

Highest Success Rate In EWS; 9% Skipped Retest

NEW DELHI: At 213 marks, NEET-UG recorded its highest ever qualifying cutoff, even as the number of candidates clearing the medical entrance examination fell by 1.15 lakh, a divergence driven by a smaller-appearing pool and a sharp upward shift in the score distribution. Moreover, the total qualified candidates for EWS and OBC for the first time breached 60% of their 'appeared' cohort, and the percentage of unreserved qualifiers now rests below 50%. The qualifying cutoffs for unreserved and EWS candidates rose to 213 from 144 in 2025 - a 69-mark jump. For OBC, SC/ST candidates, the threshold increased by 64 marks, from 113 to 177.The UR/EWS qualifying range moved from 720-162 in 2024 to 686-144 in 2025 and 715-213 this year. For OBC, SC and ST candidates, the lower end moved from 127 in 2024 to 113 last year before surging to 177.Registrations remained virtually unchanged at 22.8 lakh, compared with 22.76 lakh in 2025. But only 19.99 lakh candidates appeared, down from 22.09 lakh - a decline of nearly 2.1 lakh. Attendance consequently dropped from 97.1% to 87.7%. The number qualifying fell from 12.37 lakh to 11.21 lakh, a decline of 9.3%.Yet the success rate among those who appeared remained virtually unchanged at about 56.1%, showing that the fall in qualifiers was largely an absentee story rather than a collapse in performance. Under the category-wise qualifying criteria, UR and EWS candidates must secure at least the 50th percentile, while OBC, SC and ST candidates require the 40th percentile. For candidates with benchmark disabilities, the qualifying requirement is 45th percentile for UR/EWS and 40th percentile for OBC, SC and ST.In marks, the 2026 ranges were 715-213 for UR/EWS, 212-177 for OBC, SC and ST, 212-194 for UR/EWS-PwBD and 193-177 for most reserved-category PwBD candidates. The ST-PwBD range was 191-177. NTA's table shows 9.97 lakh candidates clearing at the UR/EWS threshold, while 81,111 OBC, 29,947 SC and 12,452 ST candidates qualified within the lower score band. These are score-band figures and not the total number qualifying from each social category.Separately, category-wise results show that 61.8% of EWS candidates who appeared qualified, the highest rate, followed by 60.7% of OBC candidates. The qualification rate was 52.4% among SC candidates, 51.2% among general candidates and 49% among ST candidates.
Article Summary: At 213 marks, NEET-UG recorded its highest ever qualifying cutoff. The qualifying cutoffs for unreserved and EWS candidates rose to 213 from 144 in 2025. For OBC, SC/ST candidates, the threshold increased by 64 marks, from 113 to 177.

Article Title: Bill seeks 3-year jail for disturbing rendition of ‘Vande Mataram’
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Anyone who prevents or disrupts the singing of Vande Mataram, which must now be sung in full at all state events and civil investiture ceremonies, could face up to three years in jail, a fine, or both under a Bill the govt plans to introduce in Parliament’s Monsoon session starting Monday.The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes to amend Section 3 of the relevant Act, which at present deals only with insults to the National Anthem , to add the national song to its ambit.“Whoever, intentionally, prevents the singing of the national anthem or the national song; or causes disturbance to any assembly engaged in such singing, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both,” states Section 3 of the proposed bill.Where a person has already been convicted, every subsequent offence shall be punishable with a minimum jail term of one year.The statement of objects and reasons for 2026 amendment bill cites the Jan 24, 1950, meeting of the Constituent Assembly, where its president Rajendra Prasad had stated that Vande Mataram, “which played a historic role in the Indian freedom struggle, shall be honoured equally with ‘Jana-Gana-Mana’ and shall have equal status with it”.“Presently, there is no specific legal provision to prevent insults to the singing of ‘Vande Mataram’,” the statement points out while justifying the need for penal provision.
Article Summary: Vande Mataram must now be sung in full at all state events and civil investiture ceremonies. Anyone who prevents or disrupts the singing of Vande Mataram could face up to three years in jail, a fine, or both under a Bill the govt plans to introduce in Parliament.

Article Title: 'Misleading the families?' AI-171 victims' kin seek black box data, memorial after AAIB affidavit
Article Text:
Air India AI-171 crash

NEW DELHI: The families of those killed in the Air India AI-171 crash have stepped up demands for the release of the aircraft's black box data and cockpit voice recorder (CVR) transcript, questioning the aircraft accident investigation bureau's (AAIB) decision to withhold the material while promising only a final investigation report.According to news agency PTI, the demands were raised at a meeting of victims' families in Ahmedabad on Sunday, days after the AAIB informed the Supreme Court that it would not disclose black box data or cockpit voice recorder recordings during the ongoing investigation.The London Gatwick-bound Air India flight AI-171 crashed shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad's Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport on June 12, 2025, when the Boeing 787 Dreamliner struck the BJ Medical College hostel complex. The crash killed 241 of the 242 people on board and 19 people on the ground, making it India's deadliest aviation disaster in decades.Romin Vahora, who lost his brother, niece and aunt in the tragedy, questioned the AAIB's decision to withhold the cockpit recordings. "If they never intended to release the data, why did they release a cockpit voice recording transcript (as part of preliminary report) just a few days after the crash?", he asked.Vahora alleged that the families wanted to know whether the selective disclosure was intended to "shift the blame onto the pilots or mislead the victims' families", PTI reported.Seeking greater transparency, he said the families wanted the raw black box data to be made public, shared directly with them or provided to their legal representatives.Vahora said the families had not initiated legal proceedings and were awaiting the final investigation report, while their lawyers continued exploring legal options to secure access to the black box data. He added that if the report was not released within the timeline indicated by the AAIB, the families would consider holding protests after obtaining the necessary permissions.Last week, the AAIB told the Supreme Court that the draft final report into the June 12 crash was expected to be ready in October. In its affidavit, the agency said there was an "absolute statutory prohibition" on releasing cockpit voice recordings and airborne image recordings, arguing that witness statements, cockpit voice recorder transcripts, air traffic control communications and medical records must remain confidential to protect the integrity of the investigation and future aviation safety inquiries.The victims' families also renewed their demand for a permanent memorial at the crash site. Vahora urged the government, Air India and the Tata group to earmark land and allocate funds for a monument honouring those who lost their lives.
Article Summary: Families of those killed in the Air India AI-171 crash have stepped up demands for the release of the aircraft's black box data and cockpit voice recorder (CVR) transcript. The demands were raised at a meeting of victims' families in Ahmedabad on Sunday. The families also renewed their demand for a permanent memorial at the crash site.

Article Title: CJP representatives to meet JP Nadda, govt reached out for talks, says party spokesperson — top developments
Article Text:
Govt opens dialogue

Police baton-charge protesters near Parliament Street, several detained

'Lathi-charge at Jantar Mantar': Kharge alleges during Monsoon Session of Parliament

Delhi Police refutes reports of violence

AAP leaders reach at Jantar Mantar

CJP activists say ready for dialogue with government, await clarity

Police use mild force to disperse CJP protesters

Gates reopened at temporarily shut Metro stations

Dipke's fast enters day 3

Wangchuk's wife says hunger strike can end on one condition

NEW DELHI: Tensions escalated in the national capital on Monday as the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Sansad Chalo' march prompted a massive police response amid heavy security during the Monsoon Session of Parliament. Protesters were allegedly baton-charged and several were detained near Parliament Street as police moved to stop the march towards the Parliament complex.Thousands of supporters had gathered at Jantar Mantar, where Opposition leaders joined the demonstration, while the government and protesters remained at odds over demands linked to the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.With prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita in force across New Delhi, Delhi Police denied permission for the march, deployed additional personnel around Parliament House and key intersections, and used force to prevent protesters from advancing towards the Parliament complex. Even as police rejected allegations of excessive force, CJP leaders maintained they were open to talks with the government, saying they were still awaiting a formal response.Here are the top developments:CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said representatives will meet Union Minister J P Nadda after the government reached out for talks. He said the party remains open to dialogue amid the ongoing 'Sansad Chalo' protest.Police baton-charged protesters participating in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Sansad Chalo' march near Parliament Street on Monday, with several demonstrators detained, according to news agency PTI.During the Monsoon Session of Parliament on Monday, Leader of the opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge raised the alleged NEET paper leak issue and claimed that a lathi-charge had taken place at the student protest at Jantar Mantar.Addressing the House, Kharge said, "This is a matter concerning students; I am speaking about the futures of lakhs of children. Thousands of students have gathered at Jantar Mantar for this cause. A lathi-charge has taken place there. The government is trying to use force, suppress voices, and drive them away."Amid social media reports of tensions at Jantar Mantar, Delhi Police on Monday dismissed claims of violence during the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest, saying reports of "sporadic use of violence/detentions" were misleading.Senior Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders, including Manish Sisodia, Sanjay Singh and Atishi, arrived at Jantar Mantar to participate in the Parliament march. Earlier Manish Sisodia had appealed to people across political affiliations to join the proposed march to Parliament, urging citizens to stand in solidarity with the country's youth.CJP activists said they are open to holding talks with the government, while maintaining that they are awaiting clarity from the authorities on the proposed dialogue.Speaking to ANI, CJP activist Saurav Das said, “The administration is trying to open talks with the government. They have come very late, but we have opened our hearts and said that we are willing to talk to them. There has been no clarity from their side as of now. The ball is in their court.”Also Read: 'They came very late': CJP claims govt reached out, but 'no clarity' on talks Delhi Police used mild force on Monday to disperse CJP protesters attempting to march towards Parliament House from Jantar Mantar. Security personnel intervened as hundreds of demonstrators moved ahead, causing traffic disruptions. Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed to maintain order and manage the situation during the Parliament session.The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) earlier on Monday closed Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat and Seva Teerth metro stations until further notice due to security concerns. However, shortly after the closure, DMRC announced that interchange facilities and gates at Rajiv Chowk and Central Secretariat stations had been reopened.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke entered the third day of his indefinite hunger strike on Monday, continuing his protest after Sonam Wangchuk was removed from the demonstration site on Saturday. He has asserted that the march will go ahead and has demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation.Amid the growing crowds, Sonam Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali J Angmo, said the activist would end his hunger strike if political leaders visited him at Safdarjung Hospital and assured him that the issue of education accountability would be raised during Parliament's Monsoon Session. Her statement came a day after Wangchuk was shifted to hospital following a medical examination.On Monday, Angmo also moved the Delhi High Court against a single-judge order refusing her plea to shift Wangchuk from Safdarjung Hospital to a private hospital of his choice.
Article Summary: CJP activists say they are open to talks with the government, but await clarity. Delhi Police deny claims of violence during Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Sansad Chalo' march. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke enters third day of indefinite hunger strike.

Article Title: Farooq Abdullah meets Wangchuk’s wife, wishes him good health
Article Text: SRINAGAR: NC president Farooq Abdullah on Sunday met fasting climate activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife Gitanjali J. Angmo, pledging support for her husband and the people of Ladakh.“May your husband get better. May he remain healthy and may his struggle be successful,” Farooq told Angmo at Delhi’s Safdarjung Hospital where he and other NC functionaries had gone to enquire about Wangchuk’s health. Angmo thanked Farooq.Farooq said he was not allowed to meet the activist who has been on hunger strike in support of Cockroach Janata Party’s demands for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over NEET paper leaks.
Article Summary: Farooq Abdullah met fasting climate activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife Gitanjali J. Angmo. Farooq said he was not allowed to meet the activist who has been on hunger strike in support of Cockroach Janata Party's demands for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

Article Title: Even as fertility rates drop, young still aspire to partnership, parenthood, shows UN report
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A first-of-its-kind survey of young adults (aged 18-39) across 73 countries, including India, by United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) shows that even as much of the world’s marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels, young people are not turning away from relationships or family life. Marriage, it says, remains “a common ideal relationship” arrangement among surveyed young adults.The report highlights that across countries — with very different demographic realities — many continue to aspire to partnership and parenthood, but say their decisions are increasingly shaped by financial security, stable employment, housing, gender equality and confidence in the future.UNFPA’s ‘Lives, Choices and Futures — Demographic Futures Survey’ 2026’ gathered perspectives of more than 1,08,000 internet connected young adults, including 1,722 respondents in India.More than two thirds of respondents selected an ideal relationship and living arrangement that includes marriage — 36% before living together and 34% after a period of cohabitation. The survey says 16% reported remaining single as their preferred living arrangement.Its findings gain significance, as across much of the world partnership formation is occurring later, marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels.“Two thirds of the world’s population now lives in a country or area where the total fertility rate is below 2.1 children per woman — the level commonly associated with the population size remaining stable over time,” the survey says.Among respondents aged 25–39, who ideally wish to marry or live with a partner, a quarter are currently single and not dating. The proportion is higher among male respondents (30% than among female respondents (19%).Financial security is the highest-rated consideration for partnership formation, cited as important by 81% of respondents. It turns out that economic and housing constraints constitute the most commonly reported category of barrier to partnership, rated important by 57%.The survey finds that among respondents — currently seeking a partner — personal networks, school or work environments, and online platforms are the most commonly reported channels for meeting potential partners, each reported by approximately one third of respondents. Overall the survey says more than 40% of respondents report spending over two hours a day on social media or the Internet for entertainment, making it the most time-intensive form of online activity examined.In India, while more than eight in 10 respondents (83%) said they feel positive or very positive about the future, nearly half of those surveyed (47%) said they are very worried about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality.While across most regional groupings of countries, two children is the most commonly reported ideal family size, the mean number of children reported by respondents aged 35–39 is lower than the mean ideal number of children reported by respondents aged 18–39.For instance, in the case of India, women aged 18-39 reported an ideal family size of 2.1 children, compared with an average of one child among women aged 35-39. Men reported an ideal family size of 2.2 children, compared with an average of 1.1 children among men aged 35-39.Parenthood is part of the future plans of most surveyed in India. Among respondents aged 35-39 in India who do not currently have children, nearly 85% said they would ideally like to become parents.
Article Summary: UNFPA’s ‘Lives, Choices and Futures — Demographic Futures Survey’ 2026’ gathered perspectives of more than 1,08,000 internet connected young adults, including 1,722 respondents in India. More than two thirds of respondents selected an ideal relationship and living arrangement that includes marriage.

Article Title: Less than half of 483 Lok Sabha MPs attended 90-100% of sittings in Parliament’s budget session, shows analysis
Article Text: NEW DELHI: As parties gear-up for taking up a wide range of issues during Parliament’s monsoon session — expected to be fiery in light of Ram temple and NEET-UG paper leak issues — the presence of MPs in both Houses is most crucial. An analysis of attendance record of the previous budget session, which ended in April, by NGO Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative shows that it is the smaller parties — with a handful of MPs — that have the highest average attendance record figures.Overall in Lok Sabha, as many as 101 MPs had signed the attendance register for all 31 sittings of the budget session — less than a quarter, or just about 21% of the 483 MPs whose attendance record was publicly available.In terms of average attendance record of parties in LS, RLP — that has one MP (Hanuman Beniwal from Nagaur — and RLD — that has two MPs (Chandan Chauhan from Bijnor and Rajkumar Sangwan from Baghpat — registered 100% attendance record for all 31 sittings. CPI(ML-L) stood second — with two of its MPs attending 30 out of the 31 sittings — as did Zoram People’s Movement with its lone MPs. Samajwadi Party took third position — with 37 of its MPs averaging attendance of 28.43 days.Overall less than one half (45.7%) of the 483 LS members had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register. The report examines the attendance record as available on the website of both Houses for the budget session to spot political party-wise trends and patterns.The single-largest party in LS, BJP (with details of 191 members available) averaged only 26.46 sittings per MP. Congress — single-largest party in opposition — averaged only 23.13 sittings (with details of 97 MPs available). Among regional political parties with more than 20 MPs during the budget session, TMC averaged only 15 sittings and DMK with 22 MPs even lesser with 14.64 sittings.In Rajya Sabha, 119 MPs — less than 46.6% of 255 MPs had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register for those many days.The top 10 political parties clocking the highest percentage of attendance are regional parties. DMDK with its lone MP (LK Sudhish) is the only one who recorded 100% attendance, followed by J&K-NC with three MPs clocking an average of 94.62%. MPs from JDS, MNF, BJD, SP, NPP and SS all recorded an average of more than 90% attendance.Despite being the largest party in the House, BJP recorded an average attendance of only 84.39% followed by Congress recording 80.66%, the report stated.
Article Summary: As many as 101 MPs had signed the attendance register for all 31 sittings of the budget session. Less than a quarter, or just about 21% of the 483 MPs whose attendance record was publicly available. RLP — that has one MP (Hanuman Beniwal from Nagaur — and RLD — that. has two MPs (Chandan Chauhan from Bijnor and Rajkumar Sangwan from Baghpat — registered 100% attendance record.

Article Title: ‘People’s safety our highest priority’: Assam govt requests Army, Air Force to remain on standby for flood evacuations
Article Text:
Morigaon: People carrying their belongings cross a flood-affected area on a boat, in Morigaon district, Assam. (PTI Photo)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: With parts of Assam continuing to reel under floods, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Sunday said the state government has requested the Army and the Air Force to remain on standby to assist in evacuating people from flood-hit districts.Sarma added that he has instructed four cabinet colleagues to rush to Upper Assam to oversee rescue and relief efforts in the three districts hit by the latest wave of floods."As the flood situation in Sivasagar, Charaideo and Jorhat continues to worsen, the Government of Assam has requested the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force to be on standby to support evacuation and rescue operations, if required," he posted.He directed ministers Ajanta Neog, Bimal Borah, Keshab Mahanta and Susanta Borgohain to immediately reach the affected areas to supervise relief efforts and ensure timely assistance reaches every affected family."The safety and well-being of our people is our highest priority. I am monitoring the situation round the clock, and we will take every necessary step to protect lives and provide all possible relief," Sarma added.Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted more rain across the northeastern states, including Assam, over the next few days.With heavy rain forecast for Guwahati and several other Assam districts over the next three to four days, the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) also urged residents to remain alert.“Daily commuters and long-distance travellers are requested to plan their routines accordingly, avoiding unnecessary movement during periods of intense rainfall.Residents in low-lying and hillside areas should stay alert for any signs of flooding or landslides,” ASDMA said in an advisory on Sunday.The body also asked local authorities to allow employees to leave early if required. It warned that moderate to heavy rain of 6cm to 12cm in 24 hours, along with thunderstorms and lightning, could worsen waterlogging, flooding, flash floods, traffic snarls and localised landslides in vulnerable areas.
Article Summary: Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has asked the Army and the Air Force to remain on standby to assist in evacuating people from flood-hit districts. He has instructed four cabinet colleagues to rush to Upper Assam to oversee rescue and relief efforts in the three districts hit by the latest wave of floods.

Article Title: 'No permission sought or granted': Delhi Police on CJP's Parliament march
Article Text:
Jantar Mantar (ANI file photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Cockroach Janta Party be allowed to march to Parliament? Yes, everyone should have the right to protest No, it's a violation of the prohibitory orders 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Monsoon Session, Delhi Police on Sunday said no permission has been sought or granted for the proposed march to Parliament called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on July 20, warning that any unauthorised gathering would invite legal action.In a statement, the police said prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the equivalent of the erstwhile Section 144 of the CrPC, are in force across the New Delhi district.Under these restrictions, protest marches, processions, demonstrations and assemblies of five or more persons are prohibited, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar and only with prior permission, the statement said.Delhi police posted: "Prohibitory orders u/s 163 BNSS are in force in New Delhi District except designated protest site at Jantar Mantar Road. Further, no permission has been sought or granted for any proposed march to Parliament on 20 July 2026. Citizens are advised not to participate in any unauthorised gathering or procession. Please respect the prohibitory orders in force and cooperate with Delhi Police in maintaining public peace, safety and security.With the Parliament session beginning on July 20, Delhi Police said elaborate security arrangements have been put in place to ensure public safety, protect vital government installations and provide security to protectees.The police warned that anyone violating the prohibitory orders would be liable for prosecution under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and other applicable provisions of law.Appealing to the public to maintain peace and order, Delhi Police urged citizens to refrain from participating in any unauthorised march or gathering and to cooperate with authorities in ensuring security during the Parliament session.Earlier, the Delhi high court upheld the Centre's decision to intervene in Sonam Wangchuk 's prolonged hunger strike after the educationist was shifted from the CJP's protest site at Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital.The court observed that the Union government's action was well within its rights and found no arbitrariness or use of force in shifting Wangchuk for medical monitoring.The move, however, triggered strong reactions from Wangchuk, his wife Gitanjali Angmo and members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). Angmo has maintained that the hunger strike continues, alleging that Wangchuk has refused to consume even oral fluids offered by the medical authorities.Meanwhile, Wangchuk's wife has vowed to lead the march to Parliament.
Article Summary: Delhi Police say no permission has been sought or granted for the proposed march to Parliament called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on July 20. Police warn that any unauthorised gathering would invite legal action. Delhi Police say elaborate security arrangements have been put in place to ensure public safety.

Article Title: 'Parliament should discuss if new anti-defection law needed': Congress' Manish Tewari after TMC, Shiv Sena (UBT) splits
Article Text:
Congress MP Manish Tewari (File photo/PTI)

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Manish Tewari on Monday called for a discussion on whether there should be a new anti-defection law, saying the current composition of the Lok Sabha no longer reflects the mandate given by voters in the 2024 parliamentary elections."The fundamental point is that in 2024, the people gave a mandate, and the Lok Sabha was constituted in accordance with that mandate. Today, two years later, the composition of the Lok Sabha is no longer in line with that mandate. It is contrary to the people's mandate," PTI quoted Tewari as saying.Speaking ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, Tewari said the "foremost priority" of the session should be for Parliament to set aside other business and debate whether a new anti-defection law is needed.The Chandigarh MP stressed the need to curb the "opportunistic politics" often described as "Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram", where politicians switch parties without regard for ideological or policy differences.Tewari also emphasised the need to distinguish and address genuine ideological or policy disagreements."A balance needs to be struck both inside and outside Parliament and state assemblies, because all these recent developments have worked to weaken Indian democracy," he said.In recent days, two parties opposed to the ruling BJP — the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and Shiv Sena (UBT) — have witnessed splits within their ranks, with some MPs either extending support to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) or joining parties already part of the NDA.In the TMC's case, three of its Rajya Sabha MPs resigned from the party, joined the BJP, and were later re-elected as BJP candidates. Meanwhile, 20 of the TMC's 28 Lok Sabha MPs merged their faction with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India and extended support to the NDA.From Shiv Sena (UBT), six of its Lok Sabha MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena, a BJP ally, reducing the Uddhav Thackeray-led party's strength in the Lower House to three members.In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the NDA won 293 seats in the 543-member House, including 240 seats secured by the BJP. The recent developments have further increased its numbers.
Article Summary: Congress MP Manish Tewari called for a discussion on whether there should be a new anti-defection law. He said the current composition of the Lok Sabha no longer reflects the mandate given by voters in the 2024 parliamentary elections. TEWari stressed the need to curb the "opportunistic politics" often described as "Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram"

Article Title: 'Avoid cloak-and-dagger tactics': Derek O'Brien writes to PM Modi on delimitation bill, seeks all-party meet
Article Text:
Derek O'Brien writes to PM Modi on delimitation bill, seeks all-party meet

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress ( TMC ) Rajya Sabha leader Derek O'Brien on Sunday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging him to convene an all-party meeting to discuss the government's proposed delimitation legislation and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment bill, describing the measures as 'draconian'.His letter comes a day before the start of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, with the opposition raising concerns over the Centre's legislative agenda.In the letter dated July 19, O'Brien said that while no delimitation-related legislation has been listed in the parliamentary bulletin for the Monsoon Session, the opposition remains apprehensive because of what he described as the government's 'dubious record' in handling important legislation.Referring to the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation bill, 2019, he alleged that the legislation was introduced in the Rajya Sabha before the supplementary list of business was circulated to MPs. He urged the government not to adopt similar 'cloak and dagger tactics' on an issue as significant as delimitation.O'Brien also referred to the Constitution (131st Amendment) bill, the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) bill and the Delimitation bill introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16 this year.He observed that the bills failed to secure the required two-thirds majority and were negatived the following day.On the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment bill, 2026, O'Brien said the legislation, which is listed for consideration and passage during the Monsoon Session, would weaken institutions working among the country's poorest and marginalised communities.He claimed that the proposed amendments would adversely affect thousands of educational institutions run by the Christian community as well as internationally reputed charitable organisations by giving the executive excessive control over their functioning.The TMC leader also stressed that Articles 19 and 26 of the Constitution must be protected.Drawing a parallel with the three farm laws that were later repealed, O'Brien urged PM Modi to convene an all-party meeting before proceeding with what he described as another instance of "cowboy legislation".The issue of delimitation has become a major political flashpoint, with several opposition parties, particularly from southern states, expressing concern that a fresh exercise based on post-2026 population figures could reduce their relative representation in Parliament despite their success in population control.The Centre, however, has maintained that no final decision has been taken on the modalities of the exercise, which cannot begin before the first Census conducted after 2026, in line with the constitutional freeze on delimitation.The proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act have also drawn criticism from opposition parties and sections of civil society, who argue that they could further tighten government oversight of non-governmental organisations and charitable institutions receiving foreign funds. The government has maintained that the changes are aimed at ensuring greater transparency and accountability in the use of foreign contributions.News agency PTI citing sources in the opposition said that TMC MPs would boycott discussions on the allocation of time for the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, during meetings of the Business Advisory Committees (BAC) of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.The party will also press for the proposed legislation to be referred to a parliamentary committee for detailed scrutiny before it is taken up for consideration and passage.
Article Summary: Trinamool Congress ( TMC ) Rajya Sabha leader Derek O'Brien on Sunday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He urged him to convene an all-party meeting to discuss the government's proposed delimitation legislation and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment bill. His letter comes a day before the start of the Monsoon Session.

Article Title: ‘No state has witnessed such a political change since Independence’: Amit Shah on Bengal
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah in Kolkata

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday described the change of guard in West Bengal as "unlike any political change since 1947", months after his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ended the Trinamool Congress' (TMC) 15-year rule in the state."The change in Bengal is unlike any political change witnessed in any state across the country since Independence," Shah said in Kolkata while virtually laying the foundation stone for a curd production plant under the Amul Bengal Dairy Project."West Bengal was once a beacon for the entire country in every field. In education, West Bengal remained decades ahead of the rest of the nation. Whether it was the freedom struggle or the country's cultural and spiritual renaissance, Bengal gave India some of its greatest leaders and freedom fighters," he added.Shah described the Left Front, which ruled West Bengal for over 30 years (1977-2011), as a "foreign ideology" and the TMC, which was in power from 2011 until it was voted out in April this year, as "corrupt and ideologically bankrupt.""First Bengal was ruled by the foreign ideology of the Left for three decades, then by the corrupt and ideologically bankrupt TMC for 15 years," the minister added in a sharp attack on the previous governments in the state.The Amul Bengal Dairy Project, he noted, would mark a milestone for the state's dairy sector and boost the income of milk producers.The Rs 700 crore project will process 30 lakh litres of milk daily and produce 10 lakh kg of curd and other cultured dairy products every day. It is expected to benefit more than 1.25 lakh dairy farmers in West Bengal, including over 30,000 women, while strengthening the cooperative dairy network in eastern India.During his three-day visit to West Bengal, Shah held discussions with the Centre and the state government officials on governance issues, including measures to curb infiltration, strengthen law and order and improve women's safety.The event marked the conclusion of Shah's three-day visit to West Bengal, during which he attended official programmes and held meetings on key issues.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah described the change of guard in West Bengal as "unlike any political change since 1947" Shah was laying the foundation stone for a curd production plant under the Amul Bengal Dairy Project. The event marked the conclusion of Shah's three-day visit to West Bengal, during which he attended official programmes.

Article Title: 'NCPI recognised by EC': Sudip Bandyopadhyay hits back after opposition's walkout over TMC rebels' presence
Article Text:
'NCPI is recognised by EC': Sudip Bandyopadhyay hits back after opposition's walkout over TMC rebels' presence

NEW DELHI: Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) leader Sudip Bandyopadhyay on Sunday defended his party's participation in the all-party meeting ahead of the Monsoon Session, saying the NCPI is recognised by the Election Commission and dismissing the oppposition's protest over the presence of rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs.His remarks came after several opposition parties staged a symbolic walkout from the all-party meeting to protest the invitation extended to Bandyopadhyay and fellow NCPI leader Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar. The opposition later rejoined the meeting, saying the walkout was meant to register its protest.Speaking to reporters, Bandyopadhyay criticised the opposition's decision to walk out."I have never seen a walkout taking place during an all-party leaders' meeting. The NCPI is recognised by the Election Commission. Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar is going to submit all documents to the Lok Sabha Speaker," he said.The former TMC leader also claimed that his erstwhile party had been reduced in strength after 20 of its Lok Sabha members joined the NCPI."I also demanded (at the all-party meeting) that a small party should not be given seats in the first row. Just eight (MPs) are left in the party (TMC) after its 20 out of 28 moved out," Bandyopadhyay told reporters.Responding to the opposition's objections over the NCPI's participation in the meeting, he said the matter would become clear once Parliament convenes."Whatever they are telling, let them say. Whatever the Lok Sabha Speaker has to say, only tomorrow the Parliament will open and you will find whose seat is where," he said.On the TMC's demand seeking the disqualification of the 20 rebel MPs, Bandyopadhyay said the decision rests entirely with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla."If the Speaker thinks that it is fit for disqualification, he will disqualify. And if he thinks that from tomorrow we should sit as a separate bloc in the first row, we'll find tomorrow. Wait for 24 hours," he said.He added that Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar would submit all the required documents to the Lok Sabha Speaker on Sunday.Dastidar welcomed the government's decision to invite the NCPI to the all-party meeting."We express our gratitude for being invited to the all-party meeting. It is a sign of respect toward our newly formed coalition of 20 MPs," she said.The all-party meeting convened by the government ahead of the Monsoon Session witnessed a symbolic walkout by opposition parties after Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla approved separate seating for the 20 rebel TMC MPs who have formed the NCPI.TMC MP Mahua Moitra questioned the government's decision to invite the rebel MPs, arguing that the Lok Sabha Speaker had not yet approved their merger and that disqualification petitions against them were still pending.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju defended the invitation, saying, "The NCPI requested recognition from the Lok Sabha Speaker; how can you ignore them? It is the government's duty to invite everyone."The NCPI held its parliamentary party meeting at Samvidhan Sadan on Sunday ahead of the Monsoon Session, which begins on Monday. While Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has approved separate seating for the 20 rebel TMC MPs.
Article Summary: Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) leader Sudip Bandyopadhyay defended his party's participation in the all-party meeting ahead of the Monsoon Session. He said the NCPI is recognised by the Election Commission and dismissed the oppposition's protest over the presence of rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs. His remarks came after several opposition parties staged a symbolic walkout to protest the invitation.

Article Title: Who will care for the child? Why many women remain outside the workforce
Article Text:
The motherhood dilemma

What the numbers say



Women and childcare

Tale of two cities



Where women earn the most

The missing childcare support



Several tasks women do

Missing childcare infrastructure

The gender gap at work



Why it matters beyond households



Women in workforce

What the data shows



Here are what infrastructural changes needed

Can you become an IAS officer while being an 'expert mother'?Can women pursue demanding careers while also fulfilling the responsibilities of motherhood? Uttar Pradesh governor Anandiben Patel believes they can and should.“Whether you become an IAS officer or a teacher, first become an expert mother. Everyone should know how to cook the food prepared at home,” Patel said at the 41st convocation of Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University.Her remarks, part of a wider message on education, family and parenting, have revived a familiar debate: what support do women have to balance careers and caregiving?Labour data suggests this balance remains difficult. For many urban women, childcare and household responsibilities, not a lack of education or ambition, remain the biggest barriers to paid work. National Statistics Office survey covering India’s 46 largest urban centres found that childcare and household responsibilities keep 69% of non-working women out of the labour force. For many women, unpaid care work remains a greater barrier to employment than education or qualifications.The gender divide is stark. Barely 1% of non-working men cite childcare or housework as the reason they are outside the workforce. Among women, it is by far the most common explanation.Even higher education hasn't solved the problem. More than 60% of women graduates are neither working nor looking for work. Only around one in ten unemployed female graduates is actively searching for a job, compared with nearly eight in ten men.For many women, the challenge isn't capability—it's compatibility between career and caregiving responsibilities.That is something Nibha Singh Mahar, an English teacher at an Army School in Ranikhet, knows firsthand. Married at 23, she became a mother at 25 and stepped away from her career for nearly two-and-a-half years to raise her child."I believe motherhood is an important responsibility, but becoming an 'expert mother' and pursuing a career are not mutually exclusive. Women should have the freedom to choose their own path. With family support, workplace flexibility and good childcare, many women successfully balance both motherhood and demanding careers," she said.She says motherhood and professional success should never be presented as competing goals."Moreover, motherhood is a beautiful journey that makes a woman feel complete in its own way, while becoming an IAS officer is undoubtedly a great achievement. A woman's worth should never be measured by choosing one over the other; she should be empowered to excel in both if she wishes," she said.The survey also shows that women's experiences differ sharply depending on where they live, suggesting structural differences rather than a uniform cultural mindset.In Howrah, 83% of non-working women say household and childcare duties keep them out of paid work. Surat follows at 81%, with Pimpri Chinchwad, Bhopal and Dhanbad not far behind.By contrast, the figure falls to 38% in Coimbatore and 41% in Agra, while Hyderabad, Visakhapatnam, Srinagar and Kota also report substantially lower numbers.The wide variation suggests that women’s participation in paid work may be influenced not only by social attitudes but also by factors such as childcare facilities, transport, workplace flexibility and local employment opportunities.The contrast between cities underlines a larger reality: childcare remains largely a private family responsibility rather than public infrastructure.India has dramatically expanded girls' access to education over the past two decades. But the systems that allow women to remain in paid employment—affordable crèches, reliable daycare centres, after-school care, safe transport and flexible workplaces—have not expanded at the same pace.For many mothers, every working day begins with the same question: who will look after the children?The experience of Kanchan Jha, a mathematics teacher at a private school in Surat, reflects that reality. She became a mother at 29 and again at 33, spending 12 years away from paid work to care for her children before returning to teaching.Asked whether she had considered leaving her job because of childcare, she says:"Like many working mothers, there have been moments when balancing work and childcare felt challenging. However, with support from family and proper planning, it is possible to continue pursuing both personal and professional goals."She recalls that the toughest phase wasn't teaching itself, but trying to do everything at once."The biggest challenge was managing time and dealing with the feeling that neither role was getting my complete attention. Balancing school responsibilities, household work, and the emotional needs of a young child required careful planning and a strong support system."Her answer to what would help more women stay employed echoes what the data suggests."Affordable and reliable childcare support would make the biggest difference. Access to quality childcare would help many mothers continue their careers while ensuring that their children receive proper care and attention."The gaps in this support system are also visible in the implementation of existing policies.The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 mandates crèche facilities in many establishments, while MGNREGA also provides for childcare at worksites. But more than 85% of India's working women are employed in the informal sector, placing them outside the maternity law's coverage. Even among establishments where crèches are mandatory, compliance remains poor. A 2019 VV Giri National Labour Institute study found that three out of four organisations with over 50 employees lacked the required childcare facilities.The challenge is particularly acute in agriculture, which employs more than 70% of working women, but where fewer than 1% receive maternity benefits. Under MGNREGA, awareness of childcare provisions remains low and their availability even lower. A survey in Rajasthan found that only 53% of women knew they were entitled to childcare facilities, while just 0.7% reported having a crèche at their worksite.Trust is another concern. Allegations of abuse at a Bengaluru daycare centre have also heightened concerns about children's safety, making many mothers even more hesitant to return to work.Women who remain in the workforce also face unequal outcomes.Across the 46 cities, salaried men earn an average of Rs 30,700 a month, compared with Rs 23,700 for women—a gap of about 23%, the NSO survey says.The disparity is wider in cities such as Kalyan-Dombivli, Navi Mumbai and Nagpur, where women earn close to half as much as men. Self-employed women fare even worse, earning less than half as much as their male counterparts.The data, however, does not suggest that women are working fewer hours. Employees across these cities work an average of nearly 50 hours a week, with salaried women in Rajkot and Faridabad among those recording the longest working hours.This is not only a question of gender equality. It is also an economic issue.India has seen a gradual rise in women's participation in the labour force. According to the latest Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), the female labour force participation rate (LFPR) for those aged 15 and above rose to 35.3% in December 2025, up from 35.1% in November. Rural female LFPR reached 40.1%, while the urban rate stood at 25.3%, highlighting the persistent gap between urban and rural India.At the same time, the NSO survey of 46 cities shows that 69% of non-working urban women cite childcare and household responsibilities as the primary reason for staying out of the workforce. Together, the two datasets suggest that while more women are entering the labour market, caregiving responsibilities continue to prevent many—particularly in urban India—from participating in paid employment.The challenge, therefore, is not simply creating jobs. It is creating the conditions that enable women to take them. Without affordable childcare, flexible workplaces and better support systems, many mothers will continue to face the same practical question each morning: who will look after the children?The survey identifies caregiving as the most commonly cited reason non-working women remain outside the labour force. Nearly seven in ten women reported it as a barrier, although the figure varied from 38% in Coimbatore to 83% in Howrah.Nibha Singh Mahar and Kanchan Jha both returned to work after taking career breaks to raise their children. They cited family support, planning, workplace flexibility and access to reliable childcare as important factors in balancing the two roles.Kanchan described affordable and reliable childcare as the measure that would make the biggest difference for working mothers.Nibha, meanwhile, said motherhood and professional success should not be treated as competing choices.“A woman’s worth should never be measured by choosing one over the other; she should be empowered to excel in both if she wishes,” she said.
Article Summary: National Statistics Office survey covering India’s 46 largest urban centres found that childcare and household responsibilities keep 69% of non-working women out of the labour force. For many women, unpaid care work remains a greater barrier to employment than education or qualifications. More than 60% of women graduates are neither working nor looking for work.

Article Title: ‘Dialogue, not silence’: Naveen Patnaik urges dialogue with students protesting exam crisis
Article Text:
'Politics aside, I urge the government to initiate a meaningful dialogue with the students who have been peacefully protesting for days,' Patnaik wrote.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support initiating a dialogue between the government and protesting students? Yes, absolutely No, I don't think it's necessary 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: BJD president and Odisha Leader of Opposition Naveen Patnaik on Sunday urged the government to initiate a meaningful dialogue with students who have been peacefully protesting for days, saying such engagement was essential to restore faith in democracy and the country’s education system.In a post on X, Patnaik said the students must be given a platform to express their concerns and called for dialogue rather than silence. “A vibrant democracy advances through dialogue, not silence—and this dialogue is most vital when it involves the youth of the nation,” he said.The BJD chief also called for the issue affecting millions of students across the country to be taken up in Parliament as a matter of the highest priority. He said a thorough debate should lead to concrete reforms to ensure that paper leaks, flawed assessments and systemic failures are not repeated, while accountability must also be fixed for the breach of trust.“Politics aside, I urge the government to initiate a meaningful dialogue with the students who have been peacefully protesting for days. They must be given a platform to express their views,” Patnaik said.He said the credibility of the examination system was central to the future of the country, warning that a failure to protect its integrity could undermine the belief that hard work and merit can help deserving students build a better future.“For millions of children in our country, education remains the only path to a brighter future,” Patnaik said, adding that India’s education system had produced generations of doctors, scientists, engineers, teachers and innovators who had contributed to the country’s development.He said the crisis went beyond a failed examination and had damaged public trust in the foundations of the education system. “A nation that compromises the integrity of its examination system, compromises its own future,” he said.Patnaik concluded by saying that sincere and open-minded engagement with peaceful youth protesters could help restore faith in democracy, education and the leadership responsible for shaping the future of young Indians.“@bjd_odisha stands firmly with the youth and students of the country,” he said.
Article Summary: BJD president and Odisha Leader of Opposition Naveen Patnaik on Sunday urged the government to initiate a meaningful dialogue with students. He said such engagement was essential to restore faith in democracy and the country’s education system. “A vibrant democracy advances through dialogue, not silence,” he said.

Article Title: Flash floods rip through Jammu and Kashmir as rain fury leaves trail of destruction - watch
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the government is doing enough to assist flood-affected residents? Yes, significantly No, not enough 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Flash floods and landslides triggered by torrential rain caused widespread devastation across Jammu and Kashmir's border districts of Poonch and Rajouri on Sunday, with rescue teams racing to reach stranded residents as the weather emergency deepened. Officials said the death toll from the rain-related disasters has risen to 11, while several people remain missing.The worst damage was reported from Surankote tehsil in Poonch district, where multiple cloudbursts, landslides and flash floods swept through villages, damaging homes and cutting off roads.Dramatic visuals from the affected areas showed vehicles being swept away by raging floodwaters, piles of mangled cars, homes collapsing under the force of the floods, and residents stranded as overflowing rivers inundated entire neighbourhoods.Multi-agency rescue teams, including the army, police, national disaster response force and state disaster response force, have been deployed to trace the missing and evacuate affected families.Union home minister Amit Shah reviewed the situation with Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha and chief minister Omar Abdullah, assuring all possible assistance from the Centre."Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah spoke with the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir, Shri Manoj Sinha, and Chief Minister Shri Omar Abdullah regarding the situation caused by heavy rainfall and assured them of all possible assistance from the Central Government," Shah's office said in a post on X.Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said the administration's immediate priority was to save lives."Since first light this morning, I've been closely monitoring the situation arising from the extremely heavy rain... the first priority of the administration is to safeguard precious lives," Abdullah said on X."The government will do everything possible to aid & assist affected people who have suffered property loss/damage due to the rains & flash floods," he added.In Rajouri, rescue teams pulled two stranded people to safety from the Muradpur area after flash floods caused water levels to rise rapidly.Deputy commissioner Abhishek Sharma told news agency PTI, "Two persons were safely rescued from the river at Muradpur, Rajouri, after they became stranded due to the flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall."Authorities have urged residents to stay away from rivers and other flood-prone areas as water levels remain dangerously high.Continuous rain since Saturday has triggered multiple cloudbursts and flash floods, washing away several structures along the Poonch River and damaging key infrastructure, with rescue and relief operations continuing across the worst-hit districts.
Article Summary: Rescue teams racing to reach stranded residents as weather emergency deepens. Death toll from rain-related disasters has risen to 11, while several people remain missing. Multi-agency rescue teams, including army, police, national disaster response force, deployed to trace missing.

Article Title: No relief for Wangchuk: Delhi HC backs government's move to shift Sonam to hospital, says no force used
Article Text:
No relief for Wangchuk: HC backs government's move to shift Sonam to hospital, says no force used

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Delhi police have transferred Sonam Wangchuk to a private hospital instead of Safdarjung? Yes, he deserves better care. No, Safdarjung is sufficient. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Sunday upheld the Centre's decision to shift climate activist Sonam Wangchuk to Safdarjung hospital, observing that the government's action was not arbitrary given his deteriorating health after weeks of fasting.Justice Mini Pushkarna, hearing a petition filed by Wangchuk's wife Dr Gitanjali J Angmo seeking his discharge from Safdarjung Hospital and transfer to a private hospital, declined to grant any interim relief.The court issued notice to the Centre and directed it to file a status report within three days."Since the government has taken the decision to shift him to the hospital on account of his medical condition, this court does not find the same to be an arbitrary action," the court observed."Since doctors at Safdarjung are closely monitoring his health and have only given oral things as per his consent, it can't be said any force is being used against him," the court added.Justice Pushkarna also took note of the government's submission that Wangchuk was not under detention. "Considering the fact that he, on his own, did not check himself into any hospital, the government was within its right to take such action," the court said, according to ANI.During the hearing, the court was informed that Wangchuk's potassium level had fallen to a dangerously low level and that intravenous (IV) fluids had not been administered because he had not consented to the treatment.The court recorded that Wangchuk would cooperate with doctors if they considered any medical intervention necessary.Clarifying its observation, Justice Pushkarna added, "Wangchuk will cooperate with doctors, if he so chooses, I am not directing."Appearing for the Centre, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said Wangchuk's health had deteriorated after 18 days of fasting in the prevailing weather conditions."Wangchuk's health was deteriorating after 18 days of fasting in the current weather," Sharma submitted, adding that prolonged fasting could lead to ketosis, shock, hypoglycaemia and impaired kidney function.He said Wangchuk was being treated in the emergency ward under the supervision of two senior doctors and referred to the latest medical reports.He also defended the credibility of the medical reports, saying tests had been conducted at Safdarjung Hospital, AIIMS, Mahajan Imaging and a private laboratory. "There is absolutely no reason for anyone to doubt the medical reports. He has been properly cared for," Sharma told the court.On the petition seeking unrestricted access for Wangchuk's family and legal counsel, Sharma said, "This is a hospital, not a courtroom." When the court asked whether attendants had been provided accommodation, a doctor informed the bench that a separate room had been arranged.The petition was filed after Delhi Police shifted Wangchuk to Safdarjung hospital on Saturday, the 21st day of his hunger strike. Appearing for Wangchuk's wife, senior advocate Kapil Sibal told the high court that the family wanted him to be shifted from Safdarjung hospital to Medanta hospital for further treatment.His wife alleged that there was no medical emergency warranting his removal from the protest site and accused authorities of taking "colourable advantage" of an earlier high court order directing medical monitoring."There existed no medical emergency or other circumstance warranting such abrupt and coercive intervention. The forcible removal was neither medically necessitated nor legally justified and constitutes a manifest infringement of Shri Sonam Wangchuk's fundamental rights," the petition stated.Angmo also claimed there were discrepancies in Wangchuk's potassium test results. The petition sought Wangchuk's immediate discharge from Safdarjung Hospital, permission to shift him to a private hospital of the family's choice, unrestricted access for independent doctors and legal counsel, and an independent medical examination.Before the hearing, Angmo posted on X that she had "full faith in the judiciary" after the Delhi high court agreed to hear the matter on an urgent basis.
Article Summary: HC backs government's move to shift Sonam to hospital, says no force used against him. Court issued notice to the Centre and directed it to file a status report within three days. Court recorded that Wangchuk would cooperate with doctors if they considered any medical intervention necessary.

Article Title: Calcutta HC halts demolition of Abhishek Banerjee's Amtala office
Article Text:
Calcutta HC orders halt to demolition at Abhishek Banerjee's Amtala office

NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Sunday directed authorities to halt all demolition work at Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Abhishek Banerjee 's office in South 24 Parganas' Amtala, until further orders.The direction came hours after an anti-encroachment drive was launched at the closed office premises amid heavy security arrangements. Officials had begun the demolition exercise as part of the anti-encroachment operation in the area.Following the high court's intervention, the demolition work has been stopped, and no further action will be taken at the site until the court issues fresh directions.A day earlier, senior Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee had alleged that the demolition of the party's Amtala office was politically motivated, asserting that the building was constructed legally on land purchased by the party after obtaining all necessary permissions.Accusing the local administration of acting in collusion with the BJP-led government, Abhishek had announced that the TMC would challenge the demolition before the Calcutta high court.The South 24 Parganas district administration had demolished the TMC MP's party office in Amtala on Saturday, claiming that the structure had been built without an approved building plan and in violation of applicable rules, according to a senior official.
Article Summary: Calcutta high court orders halt to demolition at Abhishek Banerjee's Amtala office. Officials had begun the demolition exercise as part of the anti- encroachment operation in the area. No further action will be taken at the site until the court issues fresh directions.
